# Validation of the failure classifier

<!-- Generated by scripts/evaluate_diagnosis_classifier.py from data/diagnosis_validation/; do not edit by hand. -->

Issue: #36. The classifier is `src/diagnosis/classifier.py` (docs/DIAGNOSIS.md section 5).

## 1. How the labels were made

Labels were written by hand by reading, in each run folder, the error line of the install log, the stderr log, or the status in run_report.json, and applying the category definitions of docs/PILOT_WEEK2.md section 7. `evidence` is the text that was read. The labels were written before the classifier was run on this set. They are NOT blind: the labeler had read the classifier's code (src/diagnosis/classifier.py, moved from scripts/categorize_pilot_failures.py) and had seen part of data/pilot_runs/failure_categories.json and the Pilot 4 summary before labeling.

**Consequences.** The real runs are the logs the rules were written from, so the accuracy below is an upper bound for new papers, not an estimate of it. The labeler also knew the rules. The synthetic probes (section 4) are the only part written to find gaps.

## 2. Real runs

46 stored runs (Pilots 1 to 4, the memory and CPU runs, and the first attempts kept as evidence).

| Level | Correct |
|---|---|
| Category | 46 / 46 (100.0%) |
| Name of an `OTHER` (or of a run without a failure category) | 10 / 10 (100.0%) |
| Phase in which the run stopped | 36 / 36 (100.0%) |
| All three levels | 46 / 46 (100.0%) |

No wrong answer among the real runs.

## 5. What this does not show

- Accuracy on papers outside these logs. The real set is small, comes from 12 papers, and is dominated by missing packages.
- That a category is the *cause*. The classifier reads the deciding line; a missing package can itself be the result of a pin or a platform limit (several first attempts were tool defects with the same line).
- That the labels are right. They are one person's reading of the definitions, not blind.
